0) Classic inputs (screenshot-grounded)

Full IPO walkthrough with embedded explorers: Breakdown (lean 8 stages). Bits ranks using the same three rails:

  • Metrics (Host Summary): CPU 7.23% · mem 39.12% · load ~2.35 · container mem ~64–68 MiB · limit 2 cores → negative evidence (not host saturation RCA).
  • Logs: ~7.45K Error · Watchdog Insights three ~33% outliers · same dt.trace_id KeyError cascade on DESKTOP-MBPAQK1.
  • Traces: 19.2K Error / 926 Ok · inventory GET /api/stock 500 (1.5–4.6ms) → callers 502.

1) How Bits carries a hypothesis (published loop)

Per Datadog docs, Bits runs a continuous loop of observation → reasoning → action. It does not dump all telemetry into one summarizer. It forms hypotheses, queries targeted data, then marks each lead validated, invalidated, or inconclusive and digs deeper on promising branches (Hypothesis Tree).

Step A · Seed

Take Detect context

Monitor Alert (Door A Flask High Error Rate) and/or Watchdog story / APM service page. Pull tags: service, env, version, time of alert. This is the seed — not the leaf yet.

Step B · Scope

Lock Related scope (stage 08)

Narrow to env:rca-lab-e3 · version:keyerror-…. Pick a fault window: W1 07:24:50–07:31:13Z or W2 07:45:54–07:56:42Z. Baseline = healthy traffic before 07:24:50Z — used by Detect to compare against, not as the investigation fault scope.

Step C · Hypothesize (parallel)

Generate candidate root causes

Typical ERROR candidates for this topology: (1) inventory code exception, (2) product upstream failure as root, (3) frontend-only bug, (4) infra/deploy regression, (5) noisy Watchdog false positive. Bits explores these in parallel with tool calls (metrics, traces, logs, change tracking, …).

Step D · Validate / invalidate

Query evidence per hypothesis

For each branch: does telemetry support causality or only correlation? Unsupported leads are pruned; supported leads spawn sub-hypotheses (deeper “why”) until the search space is exhausted or confidence plateaus.

Step E · Conclude

Evidence-backed conclusion or inconclusive

UI shows Investigation Steps (audit trail) and Hypothesis Tree (structure). Declare Incident remains a separate human action.

3) How 500 vs 502 get ranked (step by step · this run)

MCP aggregate for env:rca-lab-e3 status:error (from 07:24Z): roughly equal counts on all three services — so volume alone does not pick the leaf. Ranking uses position on the call path + error identity + HTTP semantics.

3.1 Observe the cascade shape

Call path — edge symptoms vs leaf
FEGET /api/checkout → 502 UpstreamProductError (edge)
ProductGET /api/product → 502 UpstreamInventoryError (mid)
LeafGET /api/stock → 500 KeyError

Leaf = deepest error span — not the first 502 the user sees.

Sample: 6a79840f…

3.2 Candidate ranking (what Bits / an SRE compares)

Rank signalInventory 500 KeyErrorProduct/FE 502 Upstream*
Trace depth Deepest error span Shallower / parent of the leaf
error.type KeyError (local exception) Upstream*Error (propagated failure)
HTTP meaning 500 = this service failed 502 = bad gateway from dependency
Log story inventory.stock.error + SKU *.upstream.error (echo of leaf)
Hypothesis verdict Promote as leaf / likely RC Demote to cascade / impact

3.3 Walk one Bits-style branch (teaching reconstruction)

  1. H1: “Frontend is the root cause” → open FE error spans → type UpstreamProductError / 502 → invalidated as root (still valid as user impact).
  2. H2: “Product is the root cause” → product spans → UpstreamInventoryError / 502 → peer points at inventory → invalidated as root; spawn sub-hypothesis on inventory.
  3. H3: “Inventory threw locally” → inventory spans → KeyError / 500 · message mentions WIDGET-1 / WAREHOUSE_SKU_INDEX → validated; deepen to code/deploy tags.
  4. H3.1: Infra/version → version:keyerror-… · container/image on fault-time inventory → corroborating, not a separate root unless change tracking shows a deploy as the trigger.
  5. Cross-check: Metrics rca.inventory.stock.errors rises with the same window; Logs @error_type:KeyError join via trace_id → hypothesis stays validated.
Counts are ~equal (~2.4k) across services — Bits (and you) must not rank by “noisiest service.” Rank by causal depth on the distributed trace.

4) Read the Hypothesis Tree on this investigation

  1. Open Hypothesis Tree.
  2. Switch also to Investigation Steps — audit of tool calls / evidence evaluations.
  3. For each branch: note validated vs invalidated. Expect inventory KeyError / 500 to survive; FE/product 502 branches to be demoted to cascade.
  4. Reject narratives about fault.injected / always-on switches (absent on this lab).
  5. Confirm infra IDs match fault-time inventory (break #1 165bbcad… or reload 3f0f94af…), not a post-heal container.

5) Corroborate with explorers (same tags)

APM: env:rca-lab-e3 status:error service:inventory @error.type:KeyError Logs: env:rca-lab-e3 @event:inventory.stock.error Metrics: sum:rca.inventory.stock.errors{env:rca-lab-e3}.as_count() Trace: https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/trace/6a79840f000000005f3c58a8cfc1f888 Bits: https://app.datadoghq.com/bits-ai/investigations/90a88d93-2570-40c6-9706-d186290ea2b6?v=tree

Name the leaf: inventory GET /api/stock · KeyError · HTTP 500 because WIDGET-1 is missing from WAREHOUSE_SKU_INDEX. Upstream 502s are ranked as cascade. Bits may package this; MTL alone is enough for the claim.
